title: How SpaceXAI is using Grok Bot to scale customer support
summary: xAI rebuilt its combined support operation around Grok Bot as Cursor's portfolio joined the company: ticket volume is up 175% with no new hires, and the bot signs into the same ticketing and issue-tracking tools the team uses. Resolution cost landed around $0.20 to $0.30, against the $1 to $4 per resolution typical of flat-rate AI support tools.

title: Introducing Grok 4.7
summary: xAI's new model for coding and knowledge work ships at the same $2 per million input and $6 per million output tokens as Grok 4.6. It was trained with a longer reinforcement-learning run weighted toward tasks that take hours, natively understands the Grok Bot harness, and leads Grok 4.6 on CursorBench 4.0, Terminal-Bench 4.0 and the Harvey legal benchmark.

title: Introducing Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0
summary: The new speech-to-text model is about twice as accurate as version 1.0 at the same price, built for flaky phone lines, competing voices and local accents rather than clean single-speaker audio. It ranks first for accuracy among 32 streaming models on Artificial Analysis, becomes the Speech-to-Text API default, and version 1.0 is deprecated in the coming weeks.

title: Memory in Grok Build
summary: Grok Build now records project conventions, decisions and facts in the background as you work, then reads them back before touching related code in a later session. Notes are stored as markdown topic files, with a /memory browser and a /dream command that consolidates recent notes.

title: Biosecurity at the frontier
summary: LatchBio's independent BioSecBench-Refusal evaluation found Grok 4.6 was the only model tested to score above 50% on both refusing disguised biohazards and completing routine biological work.

title: Setting Grok Bot loose on procurement
summary: xAI gave Grok Bot access to vendor spend, contracts, and usage data; it surfaced more than $100,000 in direct savings.

title: Designing Grok Bot for a world of persistent agents
summary: xAI published a design write-up on the Grok Bot avatar system and how the product was shaped around agents that keep running between conversations.

title: Grok Bot for Enterprise
summary: xAI made Grok Bot available to enterprises. Grok and Cursor Enterprise customers get two weeks of free usage and can invite their whole organization, including people without an existing seat.

title: A 7-step operator's manual for multi-agent Grok Bot teams
summary: A widely shared playbook (400K views) argues the single-bot era is over: build a Chief bot that routes and delegates, keep shared state in /workspace instead of chat, and gate every workflow with source, evidence, and action checks. Humans approve only money, publishing, and irreversible actions.

title: The Grok Bot PMs on persistent chats and building your first bot
summary: Two SpaceXAI product managers who ship Grok Bot walked through their own bot teams in a 47-minute interview, with the headline claim that you should never be watching a context meter. A companion guide covers bots, skills, routines, plugins, and the shared cloud computer.

title: Musk: automatic token optimization is coming to Grok Bot
summary: Elon Musk confirmed that automatic token optimization is coming to Grok Bot, part of a broader efficiency push across xAI. No percentages or pricing details yet, but the feature would cut usage costs for bot teams at the platform level.

title: Grok Bot vs Grok Automations vs Grok Build: the builder's map
summary: A comparison of xAI's three builder surfaces: autonomous bots, scheduled automations, and the free low-code Grok Build tool.

title: Grok Bot now works with X
summary: Bots can now plug into X directly, reading posts and acting inside the platform where most of the ecosystem's builders already live. Paid Grok Bot users get free X API credits to start, plus an X plugin for search, timelines, and bookmarks.

title: Grok Bot is now included with more plans
summary: Grok Bot expanded beyond the top tiers to all SuperGrok, Cursor Pro, and Cursor Teams plans. Bot usage is separate from Grok and Cursor allowances, so delegated work no longer eats a subscriber's main quota.

title: Grok 4.6 lands on Microsoft Foundry
summary: xAI's newest model becomes available through Microsoft's enterprise AI platform, a notable distribution step beyond Grok's own apps.
